packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-15 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY
Face A (overview image-001.jpg): a small irregular strip of parchment (roughly 24 x 8 cm against the scale), apparently a binding strip, with a horizontal fold/crease below the text. Only two lines of text survive, at the top edge, in a gothic textualis book hand in brown-black ink, single column as far as visible (both margins trimmed/cut; no column edge certain). A red (rubricated) initial or red-touched capital is visible mid-line 1 (before "Ueniet"?). Top line cut through at the top of the letters. A black ink blot/stain at left under line 2. The rest of the strip is blank parchment with a faint pencil shelfmark-like note and an inverted blue-ink modern note (not transcribed as text: appears to read something like "...IX/..." - modern). No running titles, glosses, or marginalia visible on the written area.
Face B: see overview image-005.jpg below.

FACE A

image-002.jpg (left tile of face A; covers the left end of both text lines; the parchment's top-left corner is folded over, hiding the beginning of both lines). Crop: crops/packet-15/img002-top.png
  002-1: [folded corner, letters seen reversed/through fold, illegible] [..]?ser?ne  (top of letters trimmed; a word ending in "-ne"/"-te" visible at right edge of tile, cut by tile edge)
  002-2: [first letter ?b/?p, then folded-over area illegible] [..]me cuius
Note: only the last two or three letters before "cuius" (read "me") are clear; what precedes is under the fold.
Below line 2: ruled line, then large black ink blot (not a letter); rest of tile blank parchment with modern pencil note "Stams ... Frag. 17a"(?) - modern, not text.

image-003.jpg (middle tile of face A; overlaps 002 at "cuius"; covers the main stretch of both lines). Crops: crops/packet-15/img003-left.png, img003-right.png
  003-1: [..]?ene ?ecbat (or ?ercbat / ?ccdbat; tops of letters trimmed at the cut, both words uncertain) z (= et) pdicabat (p with no mark visible; tops trimmed, so an abbreviation over/through p may be lost: ?p(re)dicabat) dicens. V[red stroke in V]en[...]  (cut by tile edge)
  003-2: [..]e cuius nō (= non) sum dig?tus (letters d-i-g-?-t-u-s; the fourth stroke-group may be n or i; reading ?dignus written with extra minim / ?digitus - uncertain) p(ro)cumbens (p with looped flourish through descender, read as pro-abbreviation) so[l...]  (cut by tile edge)
Punctuation: point after "dicens". Line 1 "V" capital has a red vertical stroke (rubrication touch), marking a new sentence/section.
Overlap: "cuius" on 003-2 is the same word as 002-2 "cuius".
Below text: ruling line, horizontal crease, rest blank parchment; modern pencil "...17a" (continuation of note in 002) and an inverted blue-ink modern note ("...IX..."? not transcribed further).

image-004.jpg (right tile of face A; overlaps 003 at "...ns. Ven" / "...bens so"). Crop: crops/packet-15/img004-text.png
  004-1: [dice]ns. V[red stroke]eniet fo?ra (letters f-o-?r/t-a; the third letter could be r or t; no abbreviation mark visible, but letter tops are trimmed so one may be lost) | [right column ruling; end of line]
  004-2: [p(ro)cum]bens solue (a small oblique stroke above l/u - possibly an abbreviation mark, possibly a stray stroke; read "solue" or ?solu(er)e) corri- (word broken at line end; a short oblique hyphen-like stroke follows it in the margin) |
Layout note: a vertical bounding/ruling line is visible just right of the line ends, so the right edge of the written column survives here; horizontal ruling lines above and below line 2 (ink ruling, brownish). Beyond the ruling: blank margin to the cut. Below: crease and blank parchment; no further text on face A.
Overlap: "ns. Ven" and "bens so" repeat 003.

FACE A combined (two physical lines, uncertain words marked):
  A1: [folded]?ser?ne ?ecbat z pdicabat dicens. V(red)eniet fo?ra
  A2: [b/p][folded][..]me cuius nō sum dig?tus p(ro)cumbens solue corri-

FACE B (overview image-005.jpg): the other side of the same strip, mirror-shaped. Two lines of text at the top edge in a smaller gothic textualis (smaller module than face A's two lines, which may be a larger script grade for a different text element). A red letter "V" (or "R"-like versicle sign?) in line 2 before "Congregate"; a red-touched initial at the start of line 2. Below the text: added later (?) in lighter brown/grey ink, a hand-drawn staff (one or more ruled lines with clefs at left) with neumes/square-ish notes and note-heads scattered, apparently a pen trial or added music, extending across the strip; some notes also between line 2 and the staff. Modern pencil note at lower right ("Stams ... Frag. 17v"?) - modern. A white paper/paste patch at lower right. No running title visible.

image-006.jpg (left tile of face B; shows the left edge of the written column, with a vertical ruling line at left of the text; both text lines begin here). Crop: crops/packet-15/img006-text.png
  006-1: pace in creden[...]  (cut by tile edge; "pace" with p having a descender, no abbreviation visible; line is the first surviving line, tops slightly trimmed)
  006-2: E[enlarged initial, black with red infill]x ?syon (first letter a tall long-s or h form; read syon/sion) sp̄es (stroke above: sp(eci)es?) de[...]  (cut by tile edge)
Added material in later, paler ink: a faint cross-shaped stroke between "syon" and "sp̄es" and loose pen strokes below "Ex" (not part of the text). Below line 2, in paler brown ink, rows of note-heads (oval/rhomboid shapes) along faint lines, then lower down a hand-drawn staff of about 4-5 lines with a clef-like sign at left, bar lines and short vertical strokes/notes. Looks like added music or pen trials, not the original layout; not transcribed as text.

image-007.jpg (middle tile of face B; overlaps 006 at "...n credend" / "...n sp̄es"). Crop: crops/packet-15/img007-text.png
  007-1: [i]n credendo · ut habundetis (letters h-a-b-u-n-?-e-t-i-s; the sixth letter could be d or c; ?habundetis) inspe (= in spe, written run together) z (= et) ?uirt[...] / ?uiu[...] (cut by tile edge)
  007-2: [sy]on sp̄es (= sp(eci)es?) decoris eius d̄s (d with superscript mark, = d(eu)s) manifeste ueniet. ℟ (red; R-form with diagonal stroke, read as a response sign) C[enlarged initial, black with red; continues in 008]
Punctuation: mid-height point after "credendo"; point after "ueniet". A vertical ruling line is visible just before the red ℟ / between ℟ and "C", running down into the music area (may be a column or bounding rule).
Added music below (paler ink): note-heads and a 4/5-line staff with bar lines, square/black notes at right; plus a cluster of notes at the right edge under the "C". Not transcribed.

image-008.jpg (right tile of face B; overlaps 007 at "...e z uirt" / "...et. ℟"). Crop: crops/packet-15/img008-text.png
  008-1: [insp]e z ?uirtu[...]  (minims after u ambiguous: read u-i-r-t-u; the last letter(s) lost at the torn top-right edge)
  008-2: [uen]iet. ℟ (red) C[enlarged initial, black outline with red infill]ongregate ?ill[...] / ?in[...]  (two or three minim-letters before the tear; uncertain)
The parchment is cut diagonally at the top right, so line 1 loses its end earlier than line 2. No right column edge survives on this face (the vertical ruling seen in 007 lies before ℟, so either it is a bounding rule and "℟ Congregate" runs into the margin/next column, or it is an internal ruling; uncertain).
Below text: added music in paler ink (note heads, a staff with vertical strokes, a large C-shaped clef/flourish at right); a black ink blot under "Congregate"; modern pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 17v" (modern label, not text); white paper remnant lower right.

FACE B combined (two physical lines):
  B1: pace in credendo · ut habundetis inspe z ?uirtu[...]
  B2: E(red infill)x ?syon sp̄es decoris eius d̄s manifeste ueniet. ℟(red) C(red infill)ongregate ?ill[...]

SELECTION / COVERAGE
All surviving text on both faces was read: two lines per face; no further lines survive (the rest of the strip is blank or later music/pen trials). Nothing left unread except letters hidden under the folded corner at the start of face A (lines A1-A2, tile 002) and letters lost at the trimmed tops of face A line 1 and the torn right end of face B.
Observation vs interpretation: face B line 2 has a red response-type sign (℟) before an enlarged initial, suggesting a liturgical text with responsories/versicles (interpretation only). Face A has a red-touched capital "V" mid-line after a point.

LIMITATIONS
- Folded-over corner on face A hides the beginning of both lines; unfolding or a raking-light image would help.
- Face A line 1 has letter tops trimmed; "?ecbat" and "fo?ra" are uncertain, and abbreviation marks above letters may be lost.
- "dig?tus" on face A line 2: fourth letter-group ambiguous (n vs i).
- Faces assigned A/B only by image order; recto/verso not determined from the images (modern pencil labels read "...17a"? and "17v").
- Modern pencil/blue-ink notes were not transcribed beyond noting them.
- Unverified image reading.
